# mzizi

> The canonical design system and component registry for the bundu ecosystem — a shadcn-compatible registry of UI components, hooks, library utilities, and blocks organised across the **Mzizi DNA double helix**, built on the Seven African Minerals design system. mzizi is an open-architecture project governed by the Bundu Foundation and operated by nyuchi. Install directly into any project using the shadcn CLI.

**Live:** <https://mzizi.dev>
**API:** <https://api.mzizi.dev/v1>
**MCP Server:** <https://mzizi.dev/mcp> (Streamable HTTP)
**OpenAPI 3.1:** <https://api.mzizi.dev/openapi>

Every `GET /v1/...` path below is relative to the API base above — `https://api.mzizi.dev`.
That is the canonical address of this API. The older `https://mzizi.dev/api/v1/...` form is
still served and returns identical bytes, so existing links keep working.

Every count, version, and per-node breakdown in this document is **live data**. Do not rely on a hardcoded number here — always fetch the authoritative value from the URL listed next to it. Supabase is the single source of truth.

## Live counts & version (do NOT hardcode — always fetch)

- **Total stable items:** `GET /v1/stats` → `stable`
- **Per-node breakdown:** `GET /v1/architecture` → each node's `component_count`, or MCP `list_collections`
- **Per-category breakdown:** `GET /v1/stats` → `byCategory[]`
- **Current portal version:** `GET /v1/changelog` → first row's `version` field
- **Per-type breakdown (UI / hook / lib / block):** `GET /v1/ui` → count where `type` matches
- **MCP/API usage metrics (CC BY 4.0):** `GET /v1/stats?days=7|30|90`
- **Database health:** `GET /v1/health`

## The architecture model: a DNA double helix, and nothing else

This matters for anything that reads mzizi and repeats what it says.

The frontend architecture is the **Mzizi DNA double helix**: two entwined backbones held together by cross-cutting rungs.

- An **engineering** backbone builds the product. Its strands are `core-guarantee` (the fixed contract), `shipped` (in the box, but evolves), `swappable` (the only defined fork seams), and `spine` (the harness that pre-wires everything).
- A **meaning** backbone carries the doctrine. Its strands are `genetic-code` (the Ubuntu + Bundu sequence) and `transcription` (every convention stored as queryable data).
- A **node** is a functional unit sitting on one strand. A **rung** is a base pair bridging both backbones, bound to no strand — fundi (self-healing), documentation, and discovery (SEO/AIO) are rungs.

**There are no axes, no outliers, no 3D, and no X/Y/Z.** An earlier model described "ten layers across five axes" with an "Outside" axis. It is retired, not renamed: `/v1/architecture/axes`, `/v1/architecture/frontend/axes`, `/v1/architecture/frontend/layers`, and `/v1/architecture/layers/{n}` all return **HTTP 410 Gone** with a `migrated_to` map. If you are repeating axis vocabulary about mzizi, it came from a stale source.

**Node numbers are labels, not a sequence, and the set is never capped.** Do not assume a highest node, do not enumerate a fixed range, and do not treat a gap as an error. `GET /v1/architecture` lists exactly the nodes and rungs that exist right now; more will be added. Any upper bound on a node argument is a bug — a cap of ten is what once made N11 unreachable.

There is also a separate data architecture (Pod → Relational → Document → Orchestration → Edge → Device → Open Data) served at `/v1/data-layer` and `/v1/pipeline`. **Never conflate the two models** — the helix describes frontend composition, the data layers describe storage and streaming.

## What this site is

1. A **component registry** — installable via `npx shadcn@latest add https://api.mzizi.dev/v1/ui/<name>`. Call `GET /v1/ui` for the live index or `GET /v1/stats` for counts.
2. A **design system reference** — the Seven African Minerals palette, seven heritage tones, status colours, typography, spacing, and radius tokens. Live values via `GET /v1/brand` or the `/tokens` page; the palette is generated from Supabase, so fetch it rather than copying hexes.
3. A **brand documentation hub** — canonical brand specs for bundu, nyuchi, mukoko, shamwari, nhimbe. Fetch via `GET /v1/brand`.
4. An **architecture documentation hub** — the DNA double helix (above), served at `GET /v1/architecture`, plus principles, data layer, pipeline, and sovereignty assessments.
5. An **Ubuntu doctrine surface** — Five Pillars and Five Principles at `GET /v1/ubuntu/{pillars,principles}`, rendered at `/ubuntu`.
6. An **MCP server** — AI assistants connect at `https://mzizi.dev/mcp` for the document-route registry.

## Key pages

- [Components](/components): the gallery; `/components/<name>` for one component
- [Colour tokens](/tokens): live, theme-adaptive palette and token values
- [Architecture](/architecture): the DNA double helix; `/architecture/nodes/<n>` for one node or rung
- [Playground](/playground): interactive component preview + API tester
- [Skills](/skills): published agent skills; `/skills/<name>` for one skill
- [CLI](/cli): the mzizi command-line tooling
- [Tools](/tools): the tool index
- [Ubuntu](/ubuntu): the Five Pillars and Five Principles
- [Changelog](/changelog): release history
- [Observability](/observability): live API + MCP usage metrics (CC BY 4.0)

Long-form documentation is **not** on this site. Product docs live at <https://docs.bundu.org/mzizi>; engineering docs at <https://docs.nyuchi.com>. `GET /v1/docs` and `/v1/docs/{slug}` return HTTP 410 with a `migrated_to` map.

## API endpoints (machine-readable)

All endpoints return JSON with schema.org JSON-LD metadata where applicable and permissive CORS headers.

- `GET /v1` — Discovery document
- `GET /v1/brand` — Brand system (minerals, typography, spacing, ecosystem)
- `GET /v1/ui` — Live component registry index
- `GET /v1/ui/{name}` — Individual component with inline source code (shadcn format)
- `GET /v1/ui/{name}/docs` — Component documentation (use cases, variants, a11y)
- `GET /v1/ui/{name}/versions` — Component version history
- `GET /v1/search?q=` — Cross-resource search
- `GET /v1/architecture` — The DNA double helix: nodes, rungs, and strands with live counts
- `GET /v1/architecture/nodes/{n}` — One node or rung: covenant, stakeholder, rules, count
- `GET /v1/ecosystem` — Architecture principles
- `GET /v1/data-layer` — Local-first + cloud layer specification
- `GET /v1/pipeline` — Open data pipeline (Redpanda → Flink → Doris)
- `GET /v1/sovereignty` — Technology sovereignty assessments
- `GET /v1/ubuntu/pillars` — The Five Ubuntu Pillars
- `GET /v1/ubuntu/principles` — The Five Ubuntu Principles
- `GET /v1/changelog` — Release history
- `GET /v1/changelog/{version}` — Single release
- `GET /v1/ai/instructions` — AI assistant instruction sets
- `GET /v1/ai/instructions/{target}` — Instructions by target (mcp-server, claude, copilot)
- `GET /v1/skills` — Every published agent skill (summary, no body_mdx)
- `GET /v1/skills/summary` — Same shape as `/skills`; reserved for the CLI `update` path
- `GET /v1/skills/{name}` — Single skill with full `body_mdx`
- `GET /v1/stats` — Public usage + registry counts (CC BY 4.0)
- `GET /v1/health` — Service health
- `GET /openapi` — OpenAPI 3.1 specification (YAML)

Retired, returning **HTTP 410 Gone** with a `migrated_to` map: `/v1/docs`, `/v1/docs/{slug}`, `/v1/architecture/axes`, `/v1/architecture/layers/{n}`, `/v1/architecture/frontend/axes`, `/v1/architecture/frontend/layers`.

## MCP server for AI assistants

Connect at `https://mzizi.dev/mcp` (POST, Streamable HTTP transport). A lean **document-route** server: it reads the `component_documents` store and returns whole documents, so one call gets everything about a component rather than several.

**Tools:** `list_components` (lean index, filterable by node or owner), `get_component` (one component as its full JSON document), `list_collections` (per-node collections with counts and ownership breakdown), `get_database_status` (connection health + row count).

**Resources:** `mzizi://components` (registry index), `mzizi://nodes` (per-node collection summary).

Tool and resource names are stable; the exact schema is discoverable via the standard MCP `tools/list` and `resources/list` requests — prefer discovery over trusting this list. The system prompt is loaded at startup from the `ai_instructions` Supabase table, so it stays current with the latest doctrine.

## Design system quick reference

**Seven African Minerals** — brand accents, each carrying a semantic role: **cobalt** (knowledge), **tanzanite** (identity), **malachite** (growth), **sodalite** (intelligence), **gold** (value), **terracotta** (community), **copper** (stewardship). Seven heritage tones (indigo, savanna, baobab, sunset, river, hematite, kalahari) anchor surfaces and moods.

Values are theme-adaptive and generated from Supabase — **fetch them from `GET /v1/brand` or `/tokens` rather than copying hex codes**, which drift. Consume a brand's accent through the `--brand-accent` custom property, never a literal hex.

**Typography:** Noto Sans (body), Noto Serif (display), JetBrains Mono (code). Noto Sans chosen for African language support (diacritics, broad script coverage).

**Radius:** every radius derives from a 7px unit — 7 / 12 / 14 / 17px, plus full.

**Buttons are always pill-shaped (`rounded-full`).** Touch targets: 56px default, 48px minimum. All brand wordmarks lowercase (`mzizi`, `mukoko`, `nyuchi`, `shamwari`, `bundu`, `nhimbe`).

**Install any component:**

```
npx shadcn@latest add https://api.mzizi.dev/v1/ui/button
```
